Vector Industries' First R&D Division, often referred to as simply First Division, is a major research and development department under Vector Industries. They primarily specialize in software and A.I. development, and are known among Vector staff for having highly prestigious and accomplished experts in their ranks.

Vector Industries' Second R&D Division, often referred to as simply Second Division, is a major research and development department under Vector Industries. They primarily specialize in hardware development, and often collaborate with the First R&D Division.

Vector Industries' Third R&D Division, often referred to as simply Third Division, is a major research and development department under Vector Industries. They primarily specialize in most aspects surrounding the industry of Realians.

.]] Unknown Trick Devices are special doors in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. They each feature a puzzle which must be solved to open the door and progress. Each trick device has two "eyes" which can be rotated into four different positions. Pressing L rotates the left eye, and R rotates the right. On either the top, left, right, or bottom of the eyes are two or more red pieces which are rotated along with the eye, and two or more green spaces. The goal is to place one red piece on each green space via rotating the eyes. The eyes are joined in the middle; the right of the left eye is the same location as the left of the right eye. It is possible to switch which eye a red piece is on by rotating it

WP, short for Weapon Points, are a type of point in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and Torna ~ The Golden Country. Originally codenamed Revolution, the console stood out from the competition (Sony's Playstation 3 and 's ) and by not outputting high-definition visuals and heavily pushing the concept of motion controls with the Wii remote as the default controller. The Wii was the first Nintendo console to present built-in software, also known as s. Wii Channels were displayed on the HOME Menu alongside the games, some examples are: , , , , , , or the . The Wii U is the eighth-generation home video game console released by Nintendo in 2012. The console is the direct successor to the Wii. It was announced during Nintendo's conference at E3 2011, primarily describing the features of the GamePad, a device with a touch screen, camera, and motion controls. It's called Wii U to reflect the intention of the console to be a singleplayer and multiplayer console at the same time, since "Wii" stands for "we", reflecting the multiplayer, and "U" stands for "you", reflecting the singleplayer. Whose Balloons is a minigame in Xenogears. This game can be played in the game tent located in the upper square in Bledavik, under the curtain in the middle.
